## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sirīmantajātaka* (Ja 500) is a discourse in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional framework preserved in its canonical opening, the narrative begins with the verse opening "Of wisdom full" and indicates that the "Problem of Sirimanda" is treated at greater length within the *Mahā-ummagga-jātaka* [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into at least four modern languages [SuttaCentral].

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse with the sixth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (182 matching passages totalling over 14,000 shared characters, with the longest continuous correspondence spanning segments 12.6–14.6) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring automatic alignments with Tibetan Mahāyāna texts, including the *Nāgarājābherīgāthā* (D0325) and the *Bodhisattvagocara-upāyaviṣayavikurvāṇanirdeśa* (D0146), though these machine matches are not confirmed as historical parallels by curated sources [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
